title: The Python SDK's legacy ZDX client: credentials, host and paths, token caching, and what happens when the token expires

prose.text: The Python SDK's legacy ZDX client signs in with a ZDX API key against the direct ZDX host instead of using a ZIdentity OneAPI client. It is the one Python ZDX path whose host, paths and token handling differ from OneAPI.

prose.label: Rate-limit headers.
prose.text: {{second-headers}} Retries for API calls follow the executor's general rule, [[shared.sdk-python.retries:wait-from-headers]].

checks.do: Whether a long-running Python process on the legacy ZDX client started getting 401 responses about an hour after its first sign-in; a new process signs in again.

env-and-host.statement: The legacy ZDX client takes `key_id` and `key_secret` (or `ZDX_CLIENT_ID` and `ZDX_CLIENT_SECRET`) and `ZDX_CLOUD` (default `zdxcloud`; `zdxbeta` is the other documented value), refuses to start without both credentials, and targets the host `https://api.{self._env_cloud}.net`.

quotes: raise ValueError("Both client_id and client_secret are required for ZDX authentication.")

partner-header.statement: A partner ID from the `partnerId` setting or `ZSCALER_PARTNER_ID` is added to every request as the `x-partner-id` header.

token-request.statement: It signs in by posting `key_id`, a `key_secret` equal to the hex SHA-256 of the client secret, a colon and the current epoch time, and that `timestamp`, to the host's `/v1/oauth/token`.

prefix-stripped.statement: On the legacy client the request executor strips the leading `/zdx` from each endpoint (the services build `/zdx/v1` paths) and joins the rest to the host, so data calls go to the host under `/v1`, the same prefix as the sign-in.

token-cache.statement: The client keeps tokens in a module-level `_token_cache` keyed by client ID and secret; its constructor builds the session, which calls `create_token`, and `create_token` reuses a cached token whenever one exists for the key.

no-reauth.statement: The request executor creates no OAuth handler for legacy clients (a ZDX legacy client makes the executor a legacy one), and on a 401 it re-authenticates only when one exists, so a 401 on the legacy ZDX client is returned as an error ('401 Unauthorized - token refresh attempts exhausted or OAuth not available.').

quotes: # OAuth2 setup - only for OneAPI clients, not legacy clients
if not self.use_legacy_client: self._oauth = OAuth(self, self._config) self._access_token = None else: self._oauth = None
if attempts < max_retries and self._oauth is not None:
logger.error("401 Unauthorized - token refresh attempts exhausted or OAuth not available.")
Exception("401 Unauthorized - token refresh attempts exhausted or OAuth not available."),

stale-token.statement: So once the cached token expires (ZDX tokens last 3,600 seconds), every request from that process, including from newly built legacy clients with the same credentials, gets a 401 until the process restarts.
stale-token.conditions: Read from the code at the pin: `create_token` is called only from `_build_session`, and the cache check does not look at the token's age. Not observed against a tenant.

second-headers.statement: The client reads `X-Ratelimit-Remaining-Second` only on a 429 to its sign-in and in its JWKS fetch; its general rate-limited GET helper, which also reads `X-Ratelimit-Limit-Second`, is defined but not called.
second-headers.conditions: A search of `zscaler/` at the pin finds no call to `_get_with_rate_limiting`; data requests go through the client's `send`, which reads no rate-limit header.
